minutes.headline: Board leans toward an FY27 override as the school/town budget gap sits near $3.15 million.
minutes.summary: This Select Board meeting covered several scheduled items -- a vendor-fair funding request, a car-dealer license, a sewer commission appointment, and two town-meeting warrant-article presentations (trust fund legal costs, and making Open Space a standing committee) -- before turning to the FY27 budget. The town manager reported the projected deficit had narrowed after the school department adjusted its own budget, and the board discussed timing for a possible override, a joint tri-board meeting, and budget workshops, without yet voting on an override figure.

budget_items.topic: Trust Fund Commission warrant article: appropriation for cy pres legal proceedings
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission chair asked for a general-fund appropriation to cover legal costs of court proceedings to correct outdated terms on several trust funds, including the American Legion Poor Fund. The town manager and board questioned whether the requested amount was well-founded given uncertainty about actual legal costs.

The town manager reported the deficit identified in the preliminary FY27 budget presented to the finance committee, noting it had since been reduced after the school department adjusted its own budget.
The town manager said she is currently looking at a cost-of-living adjustment for SAP employees, with further analysis underway.
The town has a policy of appropriating a set percentage of available free cash to the OPEB trust fund, to be carried on the FY27 warrant.
A fund created last year to cover unforeseen liabilities such as large vacation buyouts when an employee departs; the town manager proposed adding to it again this year.

budget_items.topic: Solid Waste Disposal Program Enterprise Fund
budget_items.what_was_said: A standing warrant article authorizing funding of the solid waste enterprise program.
The town manager said the water enterprise fund figure needs adjusting because the prior figure does not cover costs, referencing the fall special town meeting.
MRPC proposed using DTA technical-assistance funds to draft a full state planning-assistance grant application to update the housing production plan rather than doing the update directly.

budget_items.topic: School Committee FY27 needs-based restoration budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member reported the school committee's FY27 budget hearing presented a needs-based restoration budget at this total.

The fire chief presented a fourth-shift staffing proposal at a prior meeting; a board member noted it and the school budget together are expected to drive the need for an override, though no cost figure was given in these captions.

The town manager said the snow and ice deficit is not yet known and could be closed either by an in-year transfer of available funds or by free cash requiring a town meeting vote; a placeholder warrant article was included.

what_happened.line: Board members said an FY27 override warrant article will likely go forward, with the amount and structure still undecided.
The town manager reported the budget gap identified for finance committee had narrowed after the school department adjusted its own budget.
A board member linked the likely override to both the school budget and a fire department proposal for a fourth staffing shift.
Members agreed to share blackout dates to schedule a tri-board meeting, tentatively next Tuesday, and possible budget-only workshops.
No vote was taken on an override figure or on the town's FY26 goals and objectives, which was tabled until the full board is present.

why_it_matters: An override would raise property taxes above the state levy cap and would need voter approval, likely tied to town meeting.
The size of the gap depends on decisions the school department and fire department make about their own budgets, not yet finalized.
Residents who want input should watch for the tri-board meeting and any budget-only workshops, where the override amount will start to take shape.
